title: Traceability in the event log: every Event and Refusal carries the SRD rule it applies as rule="<unit id>#<clause>" (next to page=), matching the SRD[...] code tags; and wherever the engine applies a register ruling it logs ruling="R-<n>" (R-05..R-07 for Grappled are applied but not logged; check R-01..R-04 too). Game.log gets rules() and a test helper to assert a rule or ruling was applied. Backward compatible: page= stays.

history.reason: the reviewer wants detailed traceability of what the engine applied, and why
Deliberate engine-wide change (rule= and ruling= on every event and refusal); the reviewer chose one large change over a gradual migration. Lint, the full suite and the review still apply.

problems: review: rejected (The design is sound. Event.rule, Refusal.rule, and EventLog.rules()/applied()/assert_applied() are added, and a unit id matches any of its clauses. Rulings reach the d20 log through Acc.ruling, so R-06 is logged GM-only. R-05 and R-07 are logged on move, on the refusal and when the condition is added. R-01 to R-04 were already logged. The api now copies page, rule and ruling onto the 'refused' event, and page= is unchanged. It's rejected for one defect: dragging is tagged with a Grappled clause #4 that doesn't exist, while the refusal for the same Movable clause uses #3. The new tests assert #4 back, so they would pass with the wrong clause.)

review: other dungdra/combat.py:521 Moves that drag a creature are logged as rule="GLOSS.grappled#4", and so is the movement-budget refusal at line 498 and the R-05 comment at line 471. GLOSS.grappled has only three effect clauses: #1 Speed 0, #2 Attacks Affected, #3 Movable. The code has always numbered them this way (the existing SRD[GLOSS.grappled#3] tags at the drag sites) and this diff does too (the Refusal at line 406 uses "GLOSS.grappled#3" for the same Movable clause). So one clause now has two ids, and one of them doesn't exist. Anything that checks traceability with assert_applied("GLOSS.grappled#3") won't find drag events. The gate misses this because it only checks that a clause is a number.

review: test-meaningfulness tests/unit/test_combat.py:84 test_dragging_logs_the_movable_clause and test_a_tiny_grappler_dragging_a_tiny_creature_logs_ruling_r05 (and the check in test_dragging_a_creature_two_sizes_smaller_needs_no_ruling) assert the invented "GLOSS.grappled#4". They pass only because they repeat the code's own wrong constant, when they should name the SRD's Movable clause (#3).
